cases.sentence: Иван Дмитриевич ___ сидел во втором ряду кресел и глядел в бинокль на корневильские колокола.
cases.translation: Ivan Dmitrich Chervyakov sat in the second row of seats and looked through his opera glasses at the bells of Corneville.
cases.explain: "Червяков" is the subject of the verb "сидел" (was sitting), so his surname stands in the nominative case.

cases.translation: He never wrote the letter to the general.
cases.explain: The negated verb "не написал" (did not write) puts its direct object in the genitive rather than the accusative, giving "письма."

cases.sentence: Червяков кашлянул, подался туловищем вперед и зашептал ___ на ухо.
cases.translation: Chervyakov cleared his throat, leaned his body forward, and whispered to the general in his ear.
cases.explain: The verb "шептать (кому?)" takes its indirect object in the dative case, giving "генералу."

cases.sentence: Червяков сконфузился, глупо вывнулся и начал глядеть на ___.
cases.translation: Chervyakov grew embarrassed, twisted about awkwardly, and began looking at the stage.
cases.explain: The preposition "на" marking the target of his gaze governs the accusative case here, giving "сцену."

cases.sentence: Червяков нисколько не сконфузился, утерся ___ и как вежливый человек поглядел вокруг себя.
cases.translation: Chervyakov was not embarrassed in the least, wiped himself with his handkerchief, and, like a polite man, looked around him.
cases.explain: The verb "утереться (чем?)" names the instrument used without a preposition, so it takes the instrumental case: "платочком."

cases.sentence: Придя домой, Червяков рассказал жене о своем ___.
cases.translation: Having come home, Chervyakov told his wife about his mishap.
cases.explain: The preposition "о" (about) always governs the prepositional case, giving "невежестве."

reading.ru: Один прекрасный вечер, не менее прекрасный, экзекутор Иван Дмитриевич Червяков сидел во втором ряду кресел и глядел в бинокль на корневильские колокола.
reading.question: Where is Chervyakov and what is he doing at the start of the story?
options: Sitting in the second row watching a performance through opera glasses
Standing in line at a ticket booth
reading.correct: Sitting in the second row watching a performance through opera glasses
reading.explain: The text says Chervyakov sat in the second row of seats, looking through his opera glasses at the bells of Corneville.

reading.ru: Но вдруг лицо его поморщилось, глаза подкатились, дыхание остановилось.
reading.question: What happens to Chervyakov's face and breathing right before he sneezes?
options: His face wrinkles up, his eyes roll back, and his breath stops
reading.correct: His face wrinkles up, his eyes roll back, and his breath stops
reading.explain: The narrator describes his face wrinkling, his eyes rolling back, and his breath stopping just before the sneeze.

reading.ru: Чихают и мужики, и полицмейстеры, и иногда даже и тайные советники.
reading.question: What does the narrator say about who sneezes?
options: Everyone sneezes—peasants, police chiefs, even privy councillors
Only Chervyakov ever sneezes in public
reading.correct: Everyone sneezes—peasants, police chiefs, even privy councillors
reading.explain: The narrator notes that peasants, police chiefs, and even privy councillors all sneeze.

reading.ru: Он увидел, что старичок, сидевший впереди него в первом ряду кресел, старательно вытирал свою лысину из шеи перчатки и барботал что-то.
reading.question: What does Chervyakov notice about the old man sitting in front of him?
options: The old man is wiping his bald head/neck and muttering something
The old man has fallen asleep
The old man is applauding loudly
The old man has left his seat
reading.correct: The old man is wiping his bald head/neck and muttering something
reading.explain: Chervyakov sees the old man in the front row wiping his bald patch and neck and muttering something.

reading.question: What does Chervyakov realize he has done to the old man?
options: He sprayed/spat on him while sneezing
He spilled his drink on him
reading.correct: He sprayed/spat on him while sneezing
reading.explain: Chervyakov thinks to himself, "I sprayed him," realizing his sneeze hit the old man.

reading.ru: В старичке Червяков узнал статского генерала Бричалова, служащего по ведомству путей сообщения.
reading.question: Who does Chervyakov recognize the old man to be?
options: A civil general named Brizzhalov who serves in the ministry of transport/communications
His own boss at the theater
A stranger he has never seen before
reading.correct: A civil general named Brizzhalov who serves in the ministry of transport/communications
reading.explain: Chervyakov recognizes the old man as the civil general Brizzhalov, who serves in the department of ways of communication.

reading.question: How does the general initially respond to Chervyakov's apology at the theater?
options: He tells him to sit down and let him listen
He forgives him warmly and shakes his hand
He gets up and leaves the theater
reading.correct: He tells him to sit down and let him listen
reading.explain: The general brushes off the apology, telling Chervyakov to sit down and let him listen to the performance.

reading.ru: Придя домой, Червяков рассказал жене о своем невежестве.
reading.question: What does Chervyakov do when he gets home that night?
options: He tells his wife about the incident
He immediately writes a letter of resignation
He goes straight to bed without talking to anyone
He calls the general on the telephone
reading.correct: He tells his wife about the incident
reading.explain: The text says that upon coming home, Chervyakov told his wife about his mishap.

reading.ru: «А все-таки ты сходи и извинись», — сказала она.
reading.question: What does Chervyakov's wife advise him to do?
options: Go apologize to the general again
reading.correct: Go apologize to the general again
reading.explain: His wife tells him, "Still, you should go and apologize."

reading.ru: «Какие пустяки? Бог знает что! Вам что угодно?» — обратился генерал к следующему просителю.
reading.question: How does the general react when Chervyakov tries to explain himself in the reception room?
options: He brushes it off as nonsense and turns to the next petitioner
reading.correct: He brushes it off as nonsense and turns to the next petitioner
reading.explain: The general dismisses Chervyakov's explanation as nonsense and turns his attention to the next petitioner.

reading.ru: «Пошел вон!» — гаркнул вдруг посиневший и затрясшийся генерал.
reading.question: What does the general finally shout at Chervyakov after his repeated apologies?
reading.explain: The general, turning blue and shaking, suddenly barks "Get out!" at Chervyakov.

reading.ru: Придя машинально домой, не снимая вид с мундира, он лег на диван и умер.
reading.question: What happens to Chervyakov at the very end of the story?
options: He goes home mechanically, lies down on the sofa, and dies
He apologizes successfully and feels relieved
reading.correct: He goes home mechanically, lies down on the sofa, and dies
reading.explain: The story ends with Chervyakov walking home mechanically, still in uniform, lying down on the sofa, and dying.
